newsitem.title: UK: Cobalt underpinned by Shaba, no serious price hike.
newsitem.headline: Cobalt underpinned by Shaba, no serious price hike.

text.p: News that rebel fighting had spread to the north of Zaire's mineral rich Shaba region helped to underpin cobalt on Monday, though most European traders were showing a reluctance to move prices significantly higher.
"The condition in Zaire remains an important factor in the cobalt, though so far there have been no signs of production has been hit," one trader said.
On Monday a senior Zairean defence ministry official said there has been heavy fighting to hold on to the town of Kalemie.

Specking from the capital Kinshasa the official said, "Since last night there has been heavy fighting in the northern part of Kalemie. The FAZ (Zaire army) controls it but reinforcements are having to be sent in from the military base at Kamina."
Zaire produces many grades of cobalt with an annual production of around 5,000 tonnes a year.
High grade cobalt was at around $22.50 a lb, slightly up on last weeks levels.
